notes.meaning: The robe worn beneath the priest's outer vest had an opening at the top for his head, reinforced like the neck of a coat of armor. A sturdy woven collar went around the hole to keep it from tearing when put on or taken off. This ensured the sacred garment remained whole and fitting for holy service.

The craftsmen crafted ornamental pomegranates out of bright blue, purple, and scarlet yarn blended with twisted linen. These colorful decorations hung all along the bottom hem of the blue robe. They added beauty and richness to the clothing of the high priest.
The metalworkers made small bells of pure gold and placed them on the hem of the robe. These bells hung between the embroidered pomegranates along the entire lower edge.

A golden bell and an embroidered pomegranate alternated all the way around the hem of the robe. As Aaron moved about ministering inside the sanctuary, the tinkling bells let the worshippers outside know he was still alive and praying on their behalf. The workers followed every detail just as the Lord had commanded Moses.

The weavers made long tunics of woven white linen for Aaron and his sons to wear. These coats served as the main inner garments for all the priests. The clean white linen pictured the holiness and purity required of those who serve God.

The workers tailored the high priest's turban, the handsome caps for the other priests, and linen undergarments for them all. Every piece was made from finely spun linen. The undergarments ensured modesty and dignity during holy duties at the altar.

The craftsmen made the sash out of finely twisted linen, embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn. It wrapped around the waist of the priest to bind his robe for active service. Like every other item, it was finished strictly according to the Lord's instructions.

The jewelers fashioned a plate of pure gold, described as the holy crown, to be worn on the front of Aaron's turban. They carved into it like a royal seal the words: HOLY TO THE LORD. This sign reminded everyone that the high priest was set apart completely to honor God's holy name.

A blue cord was fastened to the gold plate to tie it onto the front of the turban. This held the sacred inscription in place on Aaron's forehead. The craftsmen obeyed the Lord's command to the letter.

Every part of the tabernacle, the tent where God met with His people, was now finished. The Israelites carried out the entire construction in roughly five months without cutting corners. They followed the divine pattern exactly, neither adding nor omitting anything.

The people brought the completed tabernacle pieces to Moses for inspection before setting it up. This included the fabric tent, the clasps, the wall frames, the crossbars, and the posts with their bases. Presenting the parts to Moses honored his God-given authority and allowed him to review their work.

The workers brought the protective outer layers, which were made from red-dyed ram skins and durable leather, along with the inner curtain. That inner veil was designed to screen the most holy place and shield the sacred chest from view.

The workers presented the ark of the Testimony, the carrying poles used to transport it, and the mercy seat that served as its lid. The ark held the stone tablets of God's covenant, and the mercy seat was the place where God's presence dwelled among Israel.

They brought the wooden table overlaid with gold, all of its utensils, and the Bread of the Presence. This special table held twelve loaves of bread before the Lord continually as a reminder of God's daily provision for the twelve tribes.

They brought the lampstand made of pure gold, its row of oil lamps, all its trimming tools, and the pure olive oil. These lamps were designed to be tended and lit every evening to give constant light in the sanctuary.

The workers delivered the gold altar of incense, the holy anointing oil, the fragrant incense, and the curtain for the tent doorway. These items ensured that daily prayer and worship could begin the moment the tabernacle was set up.

They brought the bronze altar for animal sacrifices, its bronze grating, its poles, and its tools, along with the bronze basin and its stand. The basin held clean water so the priests could wash their hands and feet before approaching God's presence.

The craftsmen brought the linen curtains for the surrounding courtyard, the posts, bases, ropes, and tent pegs, as well as the courtyard gate curtain. These pieces marked off the holy grounds where the worshipers could gather to bring their offerings.

They brought all the woven clothing designed for service in the sanctuary, including the special garments for Aaron the high priest and the tunics for his sons. These clothes were set aside solely for the priests' sacred duties.
The Israelites finished every single task just as the Lord had commanded Moses. Their exact obedience showed true devotion and respect for God's instructions, without inventing rules of their own.

Moses examined all the finished pieces one by one and saw that they had done everything according to the pattern God gave on the mountain. Pleased with their faithful labor, Moses commended the workers and prayed God's blessing over the entire community.
